title: Composition of etale-local logarithmic infinitesimal lifts
statement: For arbitrary log schemes with relative-section morphisms [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation], let $f:(X,L)\to(Y,M)$ and $g:(Y,M)\to(Z,N)$ have etale-local infinitesimal lifts for all fine strict square-zero tests [def-sfb-log-infinitesimal-lifting-properties]. Then their constructed composite $g\circ f$ [lem-sfb-log-morphism-operations] has the same property. The tests remain arbitrary fine log schemes without a Noetherian or saturation condition, and restriction uses the actual scheme fibre product.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; X 1.2, pp.136--139; Kato 1988 3.2--3.3. The two-stage test refinement in item proof step 2, written explicitly by F3.

proof.text: For a square of the composite, apply the property of g to the top map followed by f. Choose a witnessed etale neighbourhood V and a point over the prescribed test point. Strict etale restriction preserves fine charts. Pull back the test immersion to V; its associated inverse-image log structure is strict and the scheme immersion is still first order.

Apply the property of f to this restricted fine strict test. Compose the two etale neighbourhood maps; their chosen points give an original point in the image. Compose their strict etale log maps using the canonical restriction bijections. Identify the iterated test pullback with the test pullback for the composite neighbourhood by the product property. Both log structures are the strict pullback of the original one; the chart-and-unit formula gives the normalized identification. Associativity of log maps verifies both triangles.
